target_customer: Online platforms and marketplaces that must verify user identity at signup
problem: Platforms need to confirm that a user's government ID is real and belongs to them, quickly and with low fraud.
business_model: B2B SaaS API/SDK, usage-based ID verification

founders.name: Eric Levine
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as Visiting Group Partner at YC and later founder of Clawvisor (P26). Became SVP and head of DocV product at Socure.

founders.name: Steve Kirkham
founders.background_notes: Press describes both founders as former Airbnb Trust and Safety leaders.

technical_complexity.rationale: Document forensics and ML fraud detection needed real engineering, but the stack was standard ML and SDK work for a team with Airbnb Trust and Safety experience.

defensibility.rationale: Accuracy was the edge and a patent-pending forensics engine was claimed in 2023, yet established vendors such as Jumio, Onfido and Trulioo already sold document verification.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents kept selling competing products; Socure, an identity firm, acquired Berbix for about 70M dollars in cash and stock in June 2023.

market_need_then: Online marketplaces faced fraud and compliance pressure and manual ID review was slow; founders had seen the problem firsthand in Airbnb Trust and Safety.

branding.domain_note: berbix.com now redirects to an unrelated site, so the domain was lost after the acquisition.

identity.logo: Logo marks filed as US trademarks (serials 88574290 and 88595500); look not described in sources.
identity.voice_and_tone: Developer and conversion focused, 'convert more verified users'.

brand_strength.rationale: Trademarked and TechCrunch covered the Series A, but no sources show community or brand-led growth.

outcome_analysis: Berbix, founded by former Airbnb Trust and Safety leaders, raised a 9M dollar Series A led by Mayfield in August 2020 and sold to Socure in June 2023 for roughly 70M dollars. The founders' domain insight and developer-friendly product earned an exit, though the price is modest against the 11M raised, so it reads as a solid but not outsized outcome.
notes: Company website berbix.com redirects to an unrelated domain, treated as dead. A 2.5M seed in 2019 appears only in a Crunchbase-derived snippet, unverified. Education not found. No dated 2018 competitor coverage found; incumbents named from later comparison pages only. YC page says Mayfield-led Series A; seed investors Initialized and Fika inferred only from the Series A release.
